headline: Approved November and January meeting minutes with amendments
summary: The commission approved amended minutes from November and January meetings. Members discussed an ongoing issue at 28 Walcott Street, planned outreach events and website updates, and worked on redesigning the outreach brochure. The new Disabilities Commission chair, Chukwuka Ezewuzie, was introduced and discussed accessibility priorities for Malden.
decisions: Approved the amended November and January meeting minutes

decision_evidence.quote: the group agreed on amendments and approved the minutes with Taylor and Steve making motions and seconds.

Minutes
Approval and Amendment of Meeting Minutes: Paul led a review of the November and January
meeting minutes, with Taylor, Madelein, and others providing feedback on missing end times, privacy 
concerns, and incomplete AI-generated notes; the group agreed on amendments and approved the 
minutes with Taylor and Steve making motions and seconds.
Ongoing Case at 28 Walcott Street: Paul updated the commission on a recurring issue at 28 Walcott 
Street, noting that Marie will follow up with the problem properties unit and that relevant city 
departments and officials were copied on related communications.
Upcoming Outreach Events and Website Updates: Paul outlined plans to update the commission's 
website with information about past and upcoming outreach events, including National Night Out, 
Malden Pride, and Juneteenth, and solicited suggestions for additional events from the group

Brochure Redesign and Printing Process: Taylor, Dawn, Madelein, and Paul discussed updating the 
commission's outreach brochure, including design improvements, printing logistics, and a collaborative 
review process, with Taylor and Madelein volunteering to draft revisions and coordinate feedback.
Introduction and Priorities of New Disabilities Commission Chair: Chukwuka Ezewuzie, the new chair 
of the Disabilities Commission was introduced to the commission. Chukwuka has background in 
disability advocacy, and highlighted accessibility and inclusivity as the main priorities for 
Malden, emphasizing collaboration. Chukwuka identified accessibility as the most pressing 
disability issue in Malden, referencing global standards and the need for budget allocation to 
support access in housing, education, and other areas.
The meeting adjourned at 6:27 PM
